text:
This was supposed to be the hard week for Colorado. Nathan MacKinnon is out about a month and Cale Makar about two weeks, per Field Level Media, the Avalanche were on the second night of a back-to-back after facing Utah, and Anaheim arrived with Cutter Gauthier on a scoring tear. The Avalanche won 4-0 anyway.

The chances were close to even. Anaheim had 2.89 expected goals (the quality of the chances) to Colorado's 2.76, and replay every shot and the Ducks win slightly more often, 52% to 48%. The difference was in net. Scott Wedgewood, starting the back half of the back-to-back, stopped all 25 shots, 2.89 goals better than the chances he faced. His most important stop came five minutes in, on Gauthier, and his biggest late one was on Nikita Nesterenko's 28% look in the third.

Colorado scored eight seconds into the second period, Nicolas Roy finishing on the backhand off Nazem Kadri and Gabriel Landeskog. Then Brock Nelson took over. He scored on a power-play slap shot at 3:25 and again at 10:04 off a Martin Necas pass, and by then the Avalanche's win chance had climbed to 95%. Devon Toews added a slap shot in the third, set up by Nelson and Necas, for two points of his own. Nelson finished with two goals and an assist on just 0.27 expected goals of his own; this was finishing, not volume.

Necas had his two assists a night after taking a scary hit against Utah. Reilly, a new arrival on the blue line, made his Avalanche debut on the third pair, per the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal, and the Avs blocked 26 shots, nine more than Anaheim.

For the Ducks, Lukas Dostal allowed four on 27 shots, 1.24 more than expected, on a night when the attack did enough to score a couple. Gauthier and Mikael Granlund have driven Anaheim's headlines all month. Wedgewood just didn't let it count.
headline: Wedgewood blanks Ducks as Avalanche depth delivers
